newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks close higher on FII buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks close higher on FII buying.

text.p: Delhi stock prices recovered to close higher in late session hectic trade as domestic and foreign institutinal investors (FIIs) made heavy purchases in blue-chip stocks, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's indicative index ended 1.70 points up at 700.58 points.

Fresh buying was fuelled by Finance Minister P Chidambaram's statement that investments in primary issues would be exempted from the purview of cpaital gains in order to draw general investors back into the capital markets, brokers said.
The shares of banking firms like the State Bank of India and the Oriental Bank of Commerce, as well as BSES Ltd, were the focus of hectic activity throughout the session.
"The recovery was mainly attributed to buying by FIIs as well as domestic financial institutions but gains were confined to blue-chip counters," said Pankaj Gupta of brokers S.R. Mittal and Co.
Shares of market leader Reliance Industries rose 3.05 rupees at 187.75 and TISCO rose 1.05 rupees at 168 rupees on buying by FIIs and domestic financial houses.

Shares of the State Bank of India, the country's largest public sector banking company, firmed 3.40 rupees at 223 while shares of the Oriental Bank of Commerce ended 2.15 rupees at 73.85 on fresh purchases by domestic financial houses.
Power stock BSES firmed 5.25 rupees at 202.30 and shares of TELCO 2.25 rupees at 408.50 rupees on purchases by financial houses and Bombay-based players.
Tobacco and hotel conglomerate ITC Ltd ended 3.50 rupees up at 264.50 on speculative buying in view of the company board meeting which began on Friday.
Brooke Bond LIpton India rose 4.25 rupees at 340, IPCL 0.95 rupees at 110 and ITC HOtels 1.25 rupees at 117.25 rupees.
